comparison: Both address Nascent-Seq methodology validation (C30-C40). OpenEval finds the method SUPPORTED based on intronic reads, 5' to 3' gradient, and extension past polyadenylation sites. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, raising major concerns about sequencing depth, normalization methods, and whether differences reflect genuine biology or technical artifacts.

Both evaluate Nascent-Seq/RNA-Seq ratio as mRNA half-life proxy (C41-C45). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED based on gene ontology analysis and comparison with published half-life data. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, questioning whether quantification methods and normalization affect variance and whether intron/exon sampling biases affect ratios.

Both address rhythmic gene identification from Nascent-Seq (C24, C47). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with clear statistical criteria. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, questioning whether rhythms are truly circadian or light-driven due to LD conditions, and requesting comparisons with other labs' data for reproducibility.

Both evaluate phase distribution of rhythmic transcription (C48-C49). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED as straightforward descriptive result. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN with same concerns as R3 about circadian vs. light-driven rhythms and reproducibility.

Both address rhythmic ncRNA transcription detection (C50-C51). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with appropriate caveats about annotation limitations. Peer reviewers rate SUPPORTED, implicitly accepting ncRNA findings including pri-miRNA 122a without specific concerns.

Both evaluate poor overlap between rhythmic transcription and rhythmic mRNA (C25, C53-C54). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED as key finding directly shown in data. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, expressing major concerns about whether disconnect reflects genuine biology or technical artifacts from comparing two methods, and noting confusion about percentage calculations.

Both characterize R-R gene set with high correlations (C55-C58). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED based on correlation coefficients and reasonable inference about transcriptional regulation dominance. Peer reviewers rate SUPPORTED, not raising specific concerns and implicitly accepting these findings.

Both address known clock genes in R-R category (C59-C60). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED as method validation. Peer reviewers rate SUPPORTED as part of overall R-R characterization without specific challenges.

Both characterize R-AR gene set (C61-C64). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with clear quantification and partial mechanistic explanation via read-through transcription. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, with general concerns about normalization and technical artifacts applying to this category.

Both address central finding of AR-R genes requiring post-transcriptional regulation (C26-C27, C65-C66, C106). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED as most important result. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, identifying this as key finding but expressing major concerns about technical artifacts and requesting clarification of analysis methods.

OpenEval R10 addresses AR-R genes and post-transcriptional regulation (C65-C66). Peer R5 addresses transcriptional variability and buffering model (C65-C66, C68-C74, C107-C108). Both overlap on C65-C66. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, questioning whether variability reflects genuine biology or technical limitations.

Both evaluate transcriptional variability and rhythmic mRNA relationship (C68-C74). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with reasonable interpretation about buffering. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, questioning whether variability reflects genuine biology or technical limitations, and requesting analysis of data consistency between replicates.

OpenEval addresses AR-R genes with burst-like transcription (C75-C76). Peer R5 includes C75 in broader variability analysis. OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with reasonable speculation about mRNA stability. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN with concerns about technical vs. biological variability.

Both address miRNA involvement in selective buffering (C78-C80). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED based on miRNA target site enrichment (p<0.01), noting this is computational prediction. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, not explicitly addressing this finding but with general concerns about variance quantification applying.

Both evaluate gene ontology enrichment for high-variability AR-R genes (C81-C82). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with reasonable inference about responsiveness. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, not explicitly addressing this analysis but with concerns about technical artifacts and methods description applying.

Both characterize CLK:BMAL1 binding (C83-C90). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with clear ChIP-Seq data, E-box enrichment, and validation against published sites. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, requesting detailed read depth and mapping statistics but not explicitly challenging findings.

Both address ncRNA targets of CLK:BMAL1 (C91-C92). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with clear binding and rhythmic transcription data. Peer reviewers rate SUPPORTED, implicitly accepting ncRNA findings without specific concerns.

Both evaluate phase disconnect between CLK:BMAL1 binding and transcription (C6, C28-C29, C94-C97). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED as major finding with clear statistical significance. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, not explicitly validating but with concerns about LD vs. DD conditions and technical artifacts applying.

Both address Bmal1 knockout validation (C99-C101). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with clear differential effects supporting collaborative transcription factor model. Peer reviewers rate SUPPORTED, not raising concerns about this genetic validation providing orthogonal support.

Both evaluate motif enrichment analysis (C102). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED as computational analysis supporting collaborative binding model. Peer reviewers rate SUPPORTED, not challenging this finding as supporting evidence for collaboration hypothesis.

Both address antisense transcription at Per2 (C103-C105). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with clear strand-specific data, noting speculation about mechanism. Peer reviewers rate SUPPORTED, noting strand-specific libraries were used and not challenging the observation.

OpenEval addresses buffering model for variable transcription (C107-C108). Peer R5 includes these claims in broader variability analysis. OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with reasonable interpretation. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, questioning whether variability reflects genuine biology or technical limitations.

OpenEval evaluates supporting evidence from other studies (C109-C110), rating UNCERTAIN due to unpublished personal communication and inability to assess degree of agreement with Koike et al. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.
OpenEval addresses arguments against simple stability-based explanations (C114-C115), finding SUPPORTED with important caveats to buffering model. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.

OpenEval evaluates interpretation of binding-transcription disconnect and collaborative transcription factor model (C7, C98, C131, C137), finding SUPPORTED but noting model requires direct experimental validation. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.

OpenEval evaluates main conclusions summary (C135-C136), finding SUPPORTED as major conceptual advances: 70% of rhythmic mRNAs lack rhythmic transcription and heterogeneous transcriptional phases despite uniform binding. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.
